findings.issue_text: Exit code for 'recreate upgrade required' silently changes from 4 to 3, breaking documented exit code semantics for external consumers like automation scripts and the operator, with no compatibility handling or versioned mapping

FEATURE_DISABLED uses exit code 4, colliding with the historically documented 'recreate required' value, causing old scripts during mixed-version upgrades to misinterpret feature-disabled as a valid recreate-required verdict

Feature-gate check runs before validateConfig() in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(), so users with missing/invalid required options get 'feature not enabled' (exit code 4) instead of the correct usage error (exit code 2)

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult.java:33 may break external automation (CI scripts, operator logic) that maps exit code 4 to recreate-required, silently misinterpreting it as 'feature disabled'
picocli.exit(...) invoked as a static-style call in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:48 rather than returning an exit code from run(); confirm this is the intended Keycloak pattern
Exit code renumbering: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing consumers that parse exit code 4 as 'recreate required' (CompatibilityResult.java:31)

FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 collides with the historical meaning of exit code 4 ('recreate upgrade required'), causing old scripts to misinterpret feature-disabled failures as recreate-required and potentially tear down live deployments (CompatibilityResult.java:33)

Operator-side enforcement of the rolling-updates feature flag is not visible in the diff; no reconcile/update logic shown that passes the feature to pods or guards against the feature being missing, risking unhandled picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) failures
testFeatureNotEnabled doesn't assert the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), so an exit code regression would still pass the test (UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48)
Exit code semantics changed (recreate 4→3, 4 repurposed for feature-disabled) with no test coverage; tests assert messages but never exitCode(), so exit-code regressions would pass CI
testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and not that the exit code is 4, so wrong or zero exit codes would pass
UpdateCompatibilityMetadata's feature-disabled guard is never tested in the disabled state, so copy-paste errors in the second guard would go unnoticed
No negative test for the operator when rolling-updates is disabled, no assertion the flag propagates into build args, and no CRD-schema-level test updates for the new FeatureSpec wiring
testMissingOptionOnSave is weakened to asserting absence of 'Missing required argument', no longer verifying option validation works; a positive-path test would be better
Docs exit-code table (rows 3 and 4) has no integration test guarding the mapping, allowing docs and code to silently drift

Exit-code collision: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 with 4 repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, so existing consumers treating exit 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will silently skip the compatibility check and conclude recreation is needed

Breaking change to public constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE (4→3) in CompatibilityResult.java breaks third-party or in-tree callers compiled against the old value; diff shows no sweep of other usages of the old constant

testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest.java asserts only the error message and not the exit code, so a failed picocli.exit() path (exiting 0) would make disabled feature indistinguishable from a successful rolling-upgrade-compatible result; test should assert exitCode() == 4

Feature-disabled gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java calls printFeatureDisabled() then picocli.exit(); if picocli.exit() throws instead of setting exit code, resulting exit code 1 (software error) collides with software-error semantics

Operator behavior when the feature is disabled is only documented (advanced-configuration.adoc), not enforced in this diff — no operator-side validation or --features=rolling-updates injection, risking undefined behavior for operator users

Previously documented update-compatibility commands now fail with exit code 4 on existing production images, and since exit 4 previously meant 'recreate required', existing upgrade automation reading only the exit code will take the recreate path without complaining

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exit code for 'recreate upgrade required' silently changes from 4 to 3, breaking documented exit code semantics for external consumers like automation scripts and the operator, with no compatibility handling or versioned mapping

FEATURE_DISABLED uses exit code 4, colliding with the historically documented 'recreate required' value, causing old scripts during mixed-version upgrades to misinterpret feature-disabled as a valid recreate-required verdict

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java). Since `4` was previously the exit code for “recreate required”, existing scripts or automation written against older versions that interpret exit code `4` as “recreate required” will now misinterpret a new “feature disabled” failure (`picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` in UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata) as a valid recreate-required verdict. This is a real, diff-grounded backward-compatibility break in externally visible CLI semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-gate check runs before validateConfig() in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(), so users with missing/invalid required options get 'feature not enabled' (exit code 4) instead of the correct usage error (exit code 2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an early feature-gate in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() (before printPreviewWarning()/validateConfig()). However, the finding’s claim that this causes missing/invalid required options to return “feature not enabled” (exit code 4) instead of a picocli usage error (exit code 2) is not verifiable from the diff: required-argument/usage errors in picocli typically occur during command-line parsing before run() is invoked. The existing test for a missing required option (`testMissingOptionOnCheck`) asserts the picocli “Missing required argument” error, which would not be possible if run()’s feature check preempted parsing. The diff only shows that *validly parsed* invocations will now fail fast when the feature is disabled, which appears intentional and is even covered by the new `testFeatureNotEnabled`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult.java:33 may break external automation (CI scripts, operator logic) that maps exit code 4 to recreate-required, silently misinterpreting it as 'feature disabled'

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. This alters the CLI’s exit-code contract, and any existing external tooling that treated exit code `4` as “recreate required” would now see `4` for a different condition (“feature disabled”), as also documented in `update-compatibility.adoc`. The diff doesn’t prove such external automation exists, but the backward-incompatible change is real and could warrant compatibility notes or a preserved mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: picocli.exit(...) invoked as a static-style call in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:48 rather than returning an exit code from run(); confirm this is the intended Keycloak pattern
matched_golden_ids: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the use of `picocli.exit(...)` as problematic and suggest the preferred approach is to return an exit code instead of invoking picocli's exit helper. While the candidate emphasizes calling style/pattern and doesn’t explicitly mention that `picocli.exit()` directly triggers `System.exit()`, it identifies the same underlying concern: avoiding `picocli.exit()` in favor of returning an exit code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exit code renumbering: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing consumers that parse exit code 4 as 'recreate required' (CompatibilityResult.java:31)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does renumber `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (CompatibilityResult.java), which is an externally observable behavior change for the CLI. However, the claim that it definitively breaks “existing consumers” cannot be verified from the diff (no consumers shown), and the change appears intentional (comment referencing picocli exit codes, plus docs/test updates adding exit code 4 for feature-disabled). This is a real compatibility-impact concern, but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 collides with the historical meaning of exit code 4 ('recreate upgrade required'), causing old scripts to misinterpret feature-disabled failures as recreate-required and potentially tear down live deployments (CompatibilityResult.java:33)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (CompatibilityResult.java). This means exit code `4` no longer represents “recreate upgrade required” and now represents “feature disabled”. While there’s no internal collision after the change, it is a backward-incompatible change to the CLI exit-code contract that could cause existing external automation that historically treated `4` as “recreate required” to misinterpret a feature-disabled failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Operator-side enforcement of the rolling-updates feature flag is not visible in the diff; no reconcile/update logic shown that passes the feature to pods or guards against the feature being missing, risking unhandled picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a hard requirement that the preview feature `rolling-updates` be enabled: the CLI commands `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` now exit early with `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled, and the docs explicitly warn the operator/commands will fail otherwise. However, within the operator-related changes shown, only a test setup (`UpgradeTest`) is updated to enable the feature in the CR (`FeatureSpec.setEnabledFeatures(...)`), and a custom-image Dockerfile adds `--features=rolling-updates` at build time. There is no diff-shown reconcile/validation logic ensuring operator-managed pods are configured with the feature or preventing users from omitting it, so the concern about missing operator-side guarding/passing of the flag is a reasonable, diff-grounded completeness/scope issue, not a demonstrable bug in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled doesn't assert the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), so an exit code regression would still pass the test (UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48)

adjudication.rationale: In UpdateCommandDistTest.java, the new test `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text (`cliResult.assertError(...)`) and does not assert the process exit code. The diff adds a new dedicated exit code `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` and both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` explicitly call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`. Without an exit-code assertion in the test, a regression where the command exits with the wrong code could still pass as long as the message matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exit code semantics changed (recreate 4→3, 4 repurposed for feature-disabled) with no test coverage; tests assert messages but never exitCode(), so exit-code regressions would pass CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CLI exit-code semantics in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). However, the updated/added tests in `UpdateCommandDistTest` mostly assert output text only: `testFeatureNotEnabled` checks the error message but not `exitCode()`, and other launch-based tests likewise don’t assert exit codes for the new/changed cases. Only `testCompatible` asserts `exitCode()==0`, and there is no diff-shown test asserting the recreate-path exit code (now 3) or the feature-disabled exit code (4). This is a concrete coverage gap around the changed exit-code contract, not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and not that the exit code is 4, so wrong or zero exit codes would pass

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled`, the test only calls `cliResult.assertError("Unable to use this command...not enabled.")` and does not assert the process exit code. The implementation explicitly exits with `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` (where `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`), so a future regression to a different/zero exit code would not be caught by this test. This is a concrete test coverage gap rather than a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UpdateCompatibilityMetadata's feature-disabled guard is never tested in the disabled state, so copy-paste errors in the second guard would go unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a disabled-feature guard to UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() and UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run(). The disabled state for Metadata is explicitly tested in quarkus/tests/integration/.../UpdateCommandDistTest.java via testFeatureNotEnabled, which launches {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME} without the --features=rolling-updates flag and asserts the exact error message printed by printFeatureDisabled(). So the claim that Metadata’s guard is “never tested in the disabled state” is contradicted by the added test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative test for the operator when rolling-updates is disabled, no assertion the flag propagates into build args, and no CRD-schema-level test updates for the new FeatureSpec wiring

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new preview feature key `rolling-updates` and wires it into operator tests by always enabling it in `UpgradeTest#createInitialDeployment` via `FeatureSpec#setEnabledFeatures(...)`. There is no corresponding operator-side negative test path shown for when the feature is disabled. Similarly, the Dockerfile adds `--features=rolling-updates` to the build command, but the diff shows no test asserting this build-arg/flag propagation. The claim about missing CRD-schema-level test updates is not directly verifiable from the provided diff (no CRD schema tests are shown), but the other two points are concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concerns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testMissingOptionOnSave is weakened to asserting absence of 'Missing required argument', no longer verifying option validation works; a positive-path test would be better

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `testMissingOptionOnSave` only changes its `@Launch` arguments to include `ENABLE_FEATURE` (`--features=rolling-updates`). The assertion `cliResult.assertNoMessage("Missing required argument")` is not newly introduced or changed here, so the test is not shown as being “weakened” by this PR. The suggestion for a positive-path test is generic and not tied to a specific regression introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs exit-code table (rows 3 and 4) has no integration test guarding the mapping, allowing docs and code to silently drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes/defines CLI exit codes in `CompatibilityResult` (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE now `3`, new `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and updates the docs table in `update-compatibility.adoc` to include `m|4` and uses `m|3` for “Rolling Upgrade is not possible”. The integration test `UpdateCommandDistTest` only asserts the feature-disabled *message* (`testFeatureNotEnabled`) and asserts exit code `0` for the compatible path, but does not assert the numeric exit codes for the recreate-incompatible case (3) nor the feature-disabled case (4). So there is no test guarding the doc↔code mapping for rows 3/4, allowing drift.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exit-code collision: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 with 4 repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, so existing consumers treating exit 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will silently skip the compatibility check and conclude recreation is needed

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (and both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`/`UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` now `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled). This is a behavior/contract change for any external scripts/consumers that previously interpreted exit code 4 as “recreate required”; they would now misinterpret “feature disabled / command not usable” as “recreate required”. The diff doesn’t show internal breakage (tests/docs were updated), but it is a real compatibility concern grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking change to public constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE (4→3) in CompatibilityResult.java breaks third-party or in-tree callers compiled against the old value; diff shows no sweep of other usages of the old constant

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the public constant `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and repurposes 4 as `FEATURE_DISABLED`, which is a behavior/API contract change for anyone interpreting the CLI exit code. However, the diff also updates in-tree behavior and documentation to match (e.g., docs table now has `m|3` for the recreate case and adds `m|4` for feature-disabled; CLI commands now `exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`). The claim that there is "no sweep" of other usages cannot be verified from this snippet alone (usages may exist outside the shown hunks), so the actionable issue here is primarily the potential backward-compat impact for external tooling/scripts, not a directly verifiable in-tree defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest.java asserts only the error message and not the exit code, so a failed picocli.exit() path (exiting 0) would make disabled feature indistinguishable from a successful rolling-upgrade-compatible result; test should assert exitCode() == 4

adjudication.rationale: In UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled, the new test only asserts the error text and does not check the process exit code. The implementation now explicitly calls picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) when Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES is disabled, and FEATURE_DISABLED is defined as 4 in CompatibilityResult. Not asserting the exit code means the test would not catch regressions where the command prints the message but exits with an incorrect status.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-disabled gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java calls printFeatureDisabled() then picocli.exit(); if picocli.exit() throws instead of setting exit code, resulting exit code 1 (software error) collides with software-error semantics

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` calling `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` after printing an error. There is no evidence in the diff that `picocli.exit()` throws, nor that an exception would force exit code `1`. In fact, the diff explicitly adjusts exit codes to avoid picocli’s `1`/`2` semantics (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3`, `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). The finding relies on speculative runtime behavior not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Operator behavior when the feature is disabled is only documented (advanced-configuration.adoc), not enforced in this diff — no operator-side validation or --features=rolling-updates injection, risking undefined behavior for operator users

adjudication.rationale: The diff does more than just document the requirement: it adds the `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature flag to `Profile.Feature`, updates operator-related examples to explicitly enable it in the Keycloak CR (`spec.features.enabled: - rolling-updates` in `advanced-configuration.adoc`), updates the operator custom-image Dockerfile to build with `--features=rolling-updates`, and updates an operator integration test (`UpgradeTest`) to set `FeatureSpec.enabledFeatures` to include the new feature. While the diff does not show operator runtime validation logic, the finding’s claim that it is *only* documented and that there is no `--features=rolling-updates` injection is contradicted by the Dockerfile and test changes shown.
